# D8_TRIGDEBUG_L488784d8: per-bar intermediate values of trig_momentum_roc break_native (len 20, wd 1.0) on the _CANC swing_atr_0.25 bars, td 20261110, NY AM session plus the 300 bars before it (W-D8SPEC, relay order 1930Z)

Series: ONE continuous series of ALL bars of the row (all sessions, 2023-04 to 2026-11-13, 822,829 bars sorted by known time), built on `_CANC` bars (`/mnt/l2/l2vast/_d8spec/bars_c/swing_atr_0.25`). Rows below: bar indices 819113 to 819860 (idx = row number in the full series); the NY AM bars of 20261110 are the rows with sess = 3 and td = 20261110 (idx 819413 to 819860). I recomputed every column from the stored bars and checked: my signals over the whole series equal the module's `signal_fn` signals exactly (11672 signals; equal = True).

## Exact definitions (code: `th_grid/trig_momentum_roc.py _prep`, `_core`; `ind.ema`)
- **spb** = seconds between two bar timestamps of the BAR TABLE (not the close times): `t1` = the time of the bar's last print = for swing (leg) bars the time of the leg's EXTREME print (column t1 below; the confirming print that closes the bar is later: known UTC). spb[i] = (t1[i] - t1[i-1]) / 1e9 when bar i-1 is in the SAME session (sess_id equal), and (t1[i] - t0[i]) / 1e9 for the FIRST bar of a session, where t0[i] = the first print of that bar (for a leg bar: the confirming print of the previous leg, or the session's first print). Stored as float32 (value used = the float32 rounded to double). My recompute of spb from t0/t1 differs from the stored by at most the float32 rounding (measured: 2.5e-5 s). Values spb <= 1e-3 s or NaN are replaced by the median spb of the first 2000 bars (= 43.1963 s) before the EMA.
- **EMA200(spb)**: `ind.ema(spb, 200)`: alpha = 2/201, seeded with the FIRST spb value of the whole series (no SMA seed), recursion s = alpha*x + (1-alpha)*s over EVERY bar of the series (all sessions, no reset); the value at bar i INCLUDES bar i's own spb.
- **w** = clip(EMA200[i] / spb[i], 0.25, 4.0). **size** = median of the nonzero |close change| over bars 1..1999 = 8.0 points (constant, from the first 2000 bars, 2023-04). **k** = w / size.
- **d** = close[i] - close[i-1] (points; 0 for the first bar of the series; NOT reset at session starts). **d*k**; **q** = cumulative sum of d*k from the first bar of the series (absolute value is meaningless, only differences matter).
- **ch** = q[i] - q[i-20] (len 20 bars). **sigma** = sample std (ddof 1) of the last 60 values of dq (= d*k) INCLUDING the current (window max(len,60) = 60): `sqrt((sum dq^2 - 60 mean^2)/59)`; first valid at bar 61. **z** = ch / (sigma * sqrt(20)).
- **Event**: long when z crosses UP through +1.0 (z[i-1] <= 1.0 < z[i]), short when z crosses DOWN through -1.0 (z[i-1] >= -1.0 > z[i]); no events in the first 2000 bars. **Signal time** = the bar's known time (column known UTC). **Engine event time** = floor(known time to whole seconds) + 2 s (`ny_build.events`: `ts = t_ns // 10**9 + 2`), session filter = signal bar's session = NY AM.
- State carried in at the first row below (idx 819113): EMA200 = 188.960476 s, q = -10211.331972, spb = 50.4043.

## How much history NT8 must carry for every value to equal the engine's (plain paragraph)
Four things are history dependent. (1) The two constants of the native scaling are taken from the FIRST 2000 bars of the engine series (April 2023): size = 8.0 points and median spb = 43.1963 s; they cannot be recomputed on a live chart and must be hard-coded. (2) EMA200(spb) is seeded with the first spb of the series (2023-04-03) and run over every bar of every session without reset; its weight on the seed after N bars is 0.99005^N (0.1% after 700 bars, 0.004% after 1,000 bars), so the engine's value equals a fresh recursion only after about 1,000 bars (the swing series has roughly 1,000 bars per trading day across all sessions, so about one full trading day), which agrees to 4 digits; to match the engine to 6 digits load at least 2 trading days of ticks before the first bar you test. (3) sigma needs the last 60 dq values and ch the last 20 bars, i.e. 61 bars, and those bars continue across session boundaries (the series is not reset at 02:00, 08:30, 09:30 etc.: d is the plain close-to-close difference of consecutive bars including the jump from the last bar of the previous session to the first of the next, and the spb of the first bar of each session is t1 - t0 as defined above). (4) The swing bars themselves restart at every session boundary, so a bar series needs the previous session boundaries' bars too: for a 09:30 ET NY AM start load the pre-open sessions (pre 08:30-09:30 and London from 02:00) as well. Practical rule: start the tick processing at the beginning of the PREVIOUS trading day's Asia session (18:00 ET two days earlier) so that more than 1,000 bars precede the first NY AM bar, and hard-code size and the median spb.
